chapter: Technique, jam sessions, audiences and records
title: Smith's six-piece and big band lineups in 1938
summary: The six-piece had four rhythm and two saxes (Smith and Parker); the big band had Odell West, trumpeters Anderson and Davis, and trombonist Fred Beckett.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Talking about trumpet players, when you had this little band with Charlie Parker in it in 1938, and you had a bigger band too...
Mmm-hmm.
Buster Smith - 119
Who was the trumpet player in that six-piece band you had?
Let me see. I didn't have any in the six-piece band.
You didn't have a trumpet player?
No.
So what was the line-up, then?
We had four rhythm and Charlie and I. Just two sax.
Wasn't Odell in that band?
No. Odell was in the big band.
So who were the trumpets in the big band?

A boy called Anderson, and then a little boy called Davis (I can't think of his last name)...and who was the other trumpet player...? I forget the other trumpet player. Who was that other boy played trumpet...?
Which one of them took the solos? Who was the sort of get-off man of that lot?

Anderson [PROBABLY BUDDY ANDERSON]. And this other boy played trumpet. I forget now just who he was. But Davis played first trumpet. He wouldn't take no solos. But Anderson, he was the second trumpet player, and he'd take solos. When I went to Kansas City this last time, he wasn't around there. Neither one of them was around there. Let me see. I can't think of who the other boy was.
Buster Smith - 120
What about the trombone players?
I had Fred Beckett. I think he was with me. I didn't have but one trombone player.
The saxophones was you, Charlie, Odell...
Yeah.
Did you have a baritone?
No, we didn't have no baritone. We had three reeds.
